 

                             CITY OF NORWALK 
                   HARBOR MANAGEMENT COMMISSION 
              REGULAR MEETING MINUTES - OCTOBER 28, 2026 
                       VIA ZOOM VIRTUAL MEETING 
 

ATTENDANCE:      Jeff Mangels, Chair; Chris MacDonnell, Vice-Chair; 
                  Jon Wilkins, Secretary; Matt Gifford; Alan Kibbe; 
                  Danielle Kurkjian; Jordan Saxe 

STAFF:            Amelia Williams 

OTHERS:           Bruce Lovallo, Harbor Master; 
                  Sgt. Justin Bisceglie, Norwalk Police Marine Unit; 
  
I. CALL TO ORDER 
Chair Mangels called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. 

II. ROLL CALL 
Roll call was taken. Commissioners present are noted above and a quorum was established. 

III. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
Public participation comments are not verbatim and represent a summarization of statements 
unless otherwise noted. 
No written correspondence was received. Lynnelle Jones, 10 Point Road, commented on the 
September 23, 2026, minutes. 

IV. ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES 
A. Regular Meeting: September 23, 2026 
A correction was noted to the name of the SHIP grant. 
**    MR. MACDONNELL MOVED TO ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 
      23, 2026, AS CORRECTED. 
**    MR. KIBBE SECONDED. 
**    MOTION PASSED 6-0-1. IN FAVOR: GIFFORD, KIBBE, KURKJIAN, 
      MACDONNELL, MANGELS, SAXE. OPPOSED: NONE. ABSTAINED: 
      WILKINS. 

V. APPLICATION REVIEW 
A. Zoning Text Amendment Referral — #2026-68R 
The Commission reviewed the referral, which includes allowing warehousing as an accessory 
use to personal service establishments and revisions to the accessory dwelling unit permitting 
process, applying the same procedure to multifamily developments. 


Norwalk Harbor Management Commission 
Regular Meeting – Via Zoom 
October 28, 2026 
Page 1  

**    MR. KIBBE MOVED TO FIND ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT #2026-68R 
      CONSISTENT WITH THE HARBOR MANAGEMENT PLAN. 
**    MR. GIFFORD SECONDED. 
**    MOTION PASSED UNANIMOUSLY (7-0). 

B. Zoning Text Amendment Referral — #2026-70R 
The Commission reviewed the proposed amendment to Article 4 to allow retail sales in the SD-
MC zone, limited to properties that do not abut the harbor, with a maximum retail floor area of 
5,000 square feet as part of a mixed-use development. The Commission discussed the effect of 
non-water-dependent uses on marine commercial uses. 
**    MR. MACDONNELL MOVED TO FIND ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT #2026-
      70R INCONSISTENT WITH THE HARBOR MANAGEMENT PLAN, AS THE 
      ADDITIONAL USES ARE NOT WATER-DEPENDENT USES. 
**    MR. GIFFORD SECONDED. 
**    MOTION PASSED UNANIMOUSLY (7-0). 
Approval by the Planning & Zoning Commission will require a two-thirds supermajority vote. 
The public hearing is scheduled for November 4, 2026. 

C. 7 Twilight Place — #2026-72 CSPR Referral 
Tim DeBartolomeo, Sound Engineering Associates, presented on behalf of the property owners. 
The project includes partial demolition, raising the single-family dwelling to meet FEMA flood 
requirements, a new foundation, structural alterations, and a swimming pool. All work will be 
performed from land; no work is proposed to the seawall. Impervious coverage will be reduced. 
**    MR. MANGELS MOVED TO FIND APPLICATION #2026-72 FOR 7 TWILIGHT 
      PLACE CONSISTENT WITH THE HARBOR MANAGEMENT PLAN. 
**    MR. WILKINS SECONDED. 
**    MOTION PASSED UNANIMOUSLY (7-0). 

VI. REPORTS 
A. Chairperson 
Chair Mangels reported that the Grassy Island cleanup was completed on Saturday, October 24, 
2026, removing approximately 3,000 pounds of debris, and thanked the volunteers, organizations 
and City departments that participated. He also thanked the commissioners who attended the 
Meet the Commissioners event. 

B. Shellfish Commission 
No report. 

C. Harbor Master 
Harbor Master Lovallo reported that two moorings in the East Channel broke loose following a 
recent storm. Moorings were relabeled with owners' names; the owners have not been located, 

Norwalk Harbor Management Commission

and the moorings are being considered abandoned. He suggested a future dock at Grassy Island, 
which may be considered under Plans and Recommendations, including through a SHIP grant. 

Sgt. Bisceglie, Norwalk Police Marine Unit, had no report. 

D. Committee 
1. Mooring and Harbor Safety: Mr. Wilkins reported two transient vessels currently on moorings. 
Seasonal moorings are to be cleared by December 31. Mr. Wilkins will provide a transient 
mooring season report, with comparison to the prior season, at a future meeting. 
2. Finance: Mr. MacDonnell had no report and noted the City grant request notice is typically 
received in November. The Commission discussed outstanding invoices from Edwards Marine.
